properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 11:18PM MDT until September 23 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas,
including El Paso, Las Cruces, and the Mesilla Valley.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos,
rivers, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded, resulting in road closures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An early season back door cold front will interact with a late
season plume of deep monsoonal moisture, bringing several rounds
of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may
tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end
precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.
- A broad swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall is likely to
affect most of the Watch area between late Tuesday afternoon and
Wednesday evening, with typical, scattered monsoon season flood
impacts. However, there is increasing potential for a narrow band
of repeated thunderstorms which will result in particularly heavy
rainfall amounts, possibly exceeding 3 inches in a 6 to 12 hour
period, resulting in higher-end impacts. Forecast models
currently favor placing the focus for heaviest rainfall over the
Mesilla Valley and El Paso. But forecasts this far out,
especially when dealing with thunderstorms, are simply not
accurate enough to precisely tell yet where exactly this area of
heaviest rainfall will set up. It could just as easily shift west
or east and avoid the more populated corridor.
- http://www.weather.gov/ElPaso
properties.instruction:
The forecast will be fine-tuned and will evolve over time. You should
monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood Warnings
Tuesday afternoon and evening. The Wednesday morning commute may also
be impacted. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 1:38PM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A low pressure system will continue to affect the panhandle through
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway and Haines.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Showers will continue
to move through the area this afternoon and evening. Some of
these showers could be heavy at times

For the Skagway area, Up to an inch of rain is still possible
through this afternoon into the overnight hours tonight. The
Haines area could see anywhere from 0.5 to 1 inch of rain during
the same time period.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
